modelName: Co-ops of Whatcom County — EIP Stage Sketch
modelNote: EIP Stage Sketch of the Whatcom co-ops. E and P hold only areas a map can draw; everything that acts is an institution in I. Co-ops keep the I colour, with their border showing their kind as on the co-op map. Blue institutions govern a P area; rules are what institutions make. Only areas with a sourced tie to a co-op are drawn: relevance, not completeness. Every line’s note says where the tie came from. Every co-op on the co-op map is here, with every tie between them. Some co-ops have no E or P tie yet because none was found with a source: A1DesignBuild, Bellingham Bay Builders, Community Media Co-op, Cascadia Deaf Nation, North Coast CU, WECU, WestEdge CU, REI Bellingham, CHS Northwest. No green (E-stewarding) institution has a sourced tie to these co-ops yet. Every E and P area has its real boundary in whatcom-coops-eip-areas.geojson, and every institution with an address has a point; the RCN Map draws both (🗺 Show on map). Laws have no place, so they appear in their maker’s popup. Marc Pierson with Claude Opus 5.5, Sep 2026.

nodes.label: BMC 6.54 Taxicabs & for-hire vehicles
nodes.note: Bellingham Municipal Code chapter licensing taxicab businesses, vehicles and drivers; driver rules amended by Ordinance 2023-12-039.

nodes.label: Community to Community (C2C)
nodes.note: 1319 Cornwall Ave, Suite 101, Bellingham (moved from 203 W Holly St; Mount Vernon office too). Founded 2003 by Rosalinda Guillén. Food-sovereignty and farmworker organisation; develops farmworker co-ops. foodjustice.org.

nodes.label: Cooperativa Tierra y Libertad
nodes.note: 1240 Central Rd, Everson. Washington's first farmworker-owned co-op farm, launched 2017 on 65 acres. Berries, squash, nopales. $55,000 from the Community Food Sovereignty Fund (Food Lifeline) for a greenhouse; PCC Food Access Grant. Buyers include the Community Food Co-op, Skagit Valley Food Co-op, Bellingham Food Bank, Bellingham School District.

nodes.label: A1DesignBuild
nodes.note: 3310 Northwest Ave, Bellingham. Design/build firm dating to 1955 (roots 1928); converted to a worker co-op in 2017 with five worker-owners. Cascade Cooperatives member.

nodes.label: North Cascades Meat Producers Co-op
nodes.note: PO Box 244, Acme; farm stand at 2399 Mt Baker Hwy. Farmer-owned (Whatcom and Skagit ranchers), established 2016 (organising from 2012). USDA-inspected mobile slaughter. Founding board: Buttin' Grove Farm, Matheson Farms, Hannegan Farm and Home. Cascade Cooperatives member.

nodes.label: Puget Sound Food Hub Co-op
nodes.note: OUTSIDE WHATCOM — 15612 Best Rd, Mount Vernon. Farmer-owned; serves Whatcom through King counties, with a Whatcom aggregation drop at Cloud Mountain Farm Center, Everson. Cascade Cooperatives member.

nodes.label: Bellingham Bay Builders
nodes.note: 2111 King St, Bellingham. Worker co-op builder founded 2004. Cascade Cooperatives member.

nodes.label: Cascade Mountain Ascents
nodes.note: Worker-owned mountain-guiding collective, founded 2023. Various locations — pin is in the Mt Baker foothills. Cascade Cooperatives member.

nodes.label: Community Media Cooperative
nodes.note: Worker co-op established 2023. Location varies — pin approximate. media-coop.com. Cascade Cooperatives member.

nodes.label: Cascadia Deaf Nation
nodes.note: 4202 Meridian St #105, Bellingham. Social co-op founded 2016. Cascade Cooperatives member.

nodes.label: Cascade Cooperatives
nodes.note: Network of co-ops in Whatcom and Skagit counties, began 2014 as the Co-op Education Project, renamed 2019, incorporated as a secondary co-op in January 2022. No fixed office — pin is downtown Bellingham. cascadecooperatives.coop · (360) 441-2728. Its Google map of Whatcom & Skagit co-ops is the main source for this layer.

nodes.label: Darigold — Lynden plant
nodes.note: 8424 Depot Rd, Lynden. Dairy farmers' co-op (~250 member farms, 4 states). Its predecessor, the United Dairymen's Association, was founded in Lynden in 1918. About 95% of Whatcom dairies ship to Darigold. Not a Cascade Cooperatives member.

nodes.label: CHS Northwest (was Whatcom Farmers Co-op)
nodes.note: 402 Main St, Lynden. Whatcom Farmers Co-op merged into CHS — the national farmer-owned co-op — and now trades as CHS Northwest: farm supply, energy, agronomy for Whatcom and Skagit. Sits beside the Darigold plant; zoom in to separate the two pins.

nodes.label: Industrial Credit Union
nodes.note: Main branch 1100 N State St, Bellingham; also Sunset, Northwest Ave, Bakerview, Ferndale, Lynden, Nugents Corner. Founded 1941. Absorbed Ferndale Refinery Credit Union in 2012. Cascade Cooperatives member. Website industrialcu.com.

nodes.label: Community Food Co-op
nodes.note: Downtown store 1220 N Forest St; Cordata store 315 Westerly Rd. Founded 1970 in Fairhaven. Runs the Farm Fund — since 2000 over $878,000 to 164 local food and farm projects, including tools for the forming Nooksack Tool Co-op (2016–19). Cascade Cooperatives member.

nodes.label: Yellow Cab Co-op
nodes.note: 401 Harris Ave #222 (Fairhaven Station), Bellingham. Employee-owned since August 2023, taking over Yellow Cab of Whatcom-Skagit (founded 1992). 24-hour dispatch, all of Whatcom. Cascade Cooperatives member.

nodes.label: NW Agriculture Business Center
nodes.note: OUTSIDE WHATCOM — 419 S 1st St #207, Mount Vernon (Skagit). USDA-funded rural co-op development centre. Shown because it built two Whatcom-serving producer co-ops.

nodes.label: NW Cooperative Development Center
nodes.note: Based in Olympia; Bellingham support staff (local contact Deborah Craig). Supports new co-ops and conversions, especially home-care co-ops. Pin location approximate. nwcdc.coop · (360) 943-4241.

nodes.label: Circle of Life Caregiver Co-op
nodes.note: 1155 N State St #508, Bellingham. Founded 2009 — oldest and largest home-care co-op in Washington. In-home care for elders and disabled people. Cascade Cooperatives member.

nodes.label: North Coast Credit Union
nodes.note: 1100 Dupont St, Bellingham; also Northwest Ave and Ferndale (plus Skagit branches). Founded 1939. Cascade Cooperatives member.

nodes.label: WECU
nodes.note: 600 E Holly St, Bellingham; also Ferndale and Lynden. Founded 1936 as Whatcom Educational Credit Union. Not a Cascade Cooperatives member.

nodes.label: WestEdge Credit Union
nodes.note: 2501 James St, Bellingham. Founded 1953. Cascade Cooperatives member.

nodes.label: REI Bellingham
nodes.note: 400 36th St, Bellingham. National consumer co-op (1938); Bellingham store opened 1999.

nodes.label: Familias Unidas por la Justicia (farmworker union)
nodes.note: Independent farmworker union; Cooperativa Tierra y Libertad was formed by four of its members (USSEN 2018; Just Transition Alliance 2023).

The Co-op's general manager and meat manager took part in launching the meat co-op, and the Farm Fund paid for a Matheson Farms field day (2016–19) that covered "benefits of the cooperative model" — Matheson is a founding board farm.
